reviews.text:
I would like to raise a complaint regarding a currency display issue in the Grab app.

While I was in Malaysia, the app failed to update the currency from SGD to MYR. The fare displayed was 24, and I reasonably assumed it was RM24. However, I was subsequently charged S$24 instead.

This has resulted in a significant unexpected charge due to what appears to be a currency display or app update issue.

I would appreciate an investigation into this matter and a refund of the excess amount charged. I hope Grab will take responsibility for this issue.

reviews.title: Opacity is the name of the game
reviews.text:
I can’t remember the last time I enjoyed using Grab. The experience has become increasingly frustrating, but today was the last straw.

Grab placed a S$23.30 authorisation hold on my card while searching for a ride. Five minutes later, it told me there were no drivers and the booking failed. The failed booking isn’t available in my normal trip history for me to easily reference or dispute, while the money remains temporarily unavailable.

Then, seven minutes after telling me there were no drivers, Grab sent me a promotional notification saying “Drivers are nearby.” Thirteen minutes after that, another: “Our drivers are here and ready to pick you up.”

This sums up my experience with the app lately: increasingly poor fulfilment and opaque payment/booking information underneath relentlessly upbeat marketing designed to get me to transact again. If a booking fails, show it in my history, show the payment hold and its reversal status, and don’t immediately send me notifications claiming drivers are waiting for me.

I don’t expect every booking to succeed. I expect an app handling my money to provide a transparent record when one doesn’t.

reviews.title: Greedy app taking advantage of hard working drivers
reviews.text:
I am writing to formally complain about Grab Vietnam’s current fee and commission structure and the way it is affecting Grab drivers.

Grab drivers are the people doing the actual work — spending hours on the road, paying for gasoline, vehicle maintenance, insurance, repairs, depreciation, and taking on the risks of driving passengers every day. Yet Grab continues taking a significant portion of the fare, leaving drivers with an increasingly small amount for the actual work they perform.

This is extremely concerning when drivers can complete a trip where the passenger pays a substantial fare, but after Grab’s deductions, the driver receives only a fraction of that amount. After fuel and vehicle expenses are taken out, some drivers may be left with almost nothing.

A technology platform should not build its business by continuously increasing the financial burden on the people who make the platform possible.

Drivers should not have to work longer hours simply to compensate for an increasingly aggressive platform fee structure.

Grab needs to remember that without drivers, there is no Grab transportation business.

I respectfully request that Grab Vietnam review this fee structure, increase transparency, and establish a fairer revenue-sharing model that allows drivers to earn a reasonable income from the work they perform.

Please treat this as a formal complaint and provide me with a written response explaining Grab Vietnam’s position and what actions, if any, will be taken.

reviews.text:
我在越南使用 Grab 多年，但这次 GrabMart 的体验让我非常失望。

我于 14:15 在 LOTTE MART 下单，App 显示预计 15:10–15:25 送达。然而超过预计时间很久，Grab 一直没有安排到配送司机，订单却仍然显示“准时（On time）”。

我主动联系 Grab 客服，希望他们协助解决配送问题，但得到的主要解决方案竟然只是让我自己取消订单，没有提供任何实际的解决办法。

在我等待了很长时间之后，Grab 最终又因为“配送时间太长”主动取消了订单。也就是说，平台无法完成已经接受的订单，却让消费者承担长时间等待带来的时间成本和不便。

退款当然应该退，但退款并不能解决整个服务体验的问题。我还使用了多个优惠，而且整个过程中最让我不满意的是：

为什么已经严重超过预计送达时间，系统仍然显示“准时”？为什么平台无法安排配送时，客服唯一能提供的方案是让消费者自己取消订单？

我已经向 Grab 提交正式投诉，工单目前仍在处理中。

作为一个提供打车、外卖和购物服务的大型平台，我认为 Grab 至少应该提供准确透明的订单状态，以及在服务失败时真正能够解决问题的客服，而不是让消费者长时间等待之后自行承担结果。

目前只能给 1 星。希望 Grab 能认真改善配送机制和客户服务，而不只是道歉、退款然后结束问题。

I purchased the Grab Travel Pass expecting to receive better prices and exclusive discounts. Unfortunately, my experience has been the exact opposite.

To test whether the Travel Pass was actually providing any benefit, I compared the price of the same airport ride at the same time on my account and on my friend’s account. Surprisingly, my fare was consistently higher, despite me paying for a program that is supposed to offer savings. This was not a one-time occurrence. I have noticed the same pattern multiple times, both for rides and food delivery orders.

What exactly is the advantage of paying for a discount program if the final prices on my account are often more expensive than on an account without those benefits?

As a customer, this feels misleading and extremely frustrating. The platform promotes savings, but my experience suggests that the advertised discounts do not necessarily translate into lower prices. In practice, I have ended up paying more than someone using a regular account.

I believe Grab should be more transparent about how prices and discounts are calculated. Until there is greater clarity, I cannot recommend purchasing the Travel Pass. Based on my experience, it simply did not deliver the value it promised.

reviews.text: I have been a Grab Taxi user for three years. At first the service was excellent. But my most recent trip to Thailand reveals that the taxi side of Grab is failing fast. Any time of the day or night, the app will tell you it’s a busy time and there aren’t many drivers on the road. It takes ages for a driver to accept. Waiting times are nearly always in double figures. About half the rides I have booked on this trip have been cancelled by the driver with no reason given. I’ve had rides accepted by the driver who has then driven off in the opposite direction, drivers fail to answer calls or reply to messages, the app states the driver has arrived, but there is no driver within five kilometres of me. It is chaotic and cannot be relied upon any longer, if you are a user that has to get from A to B. A pity, because it has been great in the past. But no longer.

We ordered the extra large car because of this anyway and paid extra so we would have enough space. I had one small bag I was going to put on my lap as he was moaning about the bags at the back, and he canceled the ride on us, in the rain with 2 small crying children and my wife with a broken leg. My wife pleaded with him but he didn’t care. He made me unload all my luggage and wheelchair next to the road and drove off. I was furious and he is clearly a heartless prick. reviews.title: Unreliable map locations; no Help
reviews.text:
If you're taking a Grab to a new place, it pays to double-check the location the Grab map chooses against the actual location on Google or Apple maps. This may prevent you being dropped somewhere miles away in the wrong direction, then having to order another Grab to take you to the correct location because Grab has it wrong.

The app makes it VERY DIFFICULT to check whether the destination is correct because it only lists a street address for the pickup point, not the drop off. The destination is just a big red pin on a vague map.

Also there is no help once you're dumped at the wrong place.

This happened to me. After several fruitless phone calls Grab eventually sent me an email asking for the correct location of the business, which I provided. I expected to get a refund for the two totally unnecessary time-wasting trips but instead they sent an email reply arguing they had dropped me within 0.002km of the destination. No, you did not.

reviews.title: Not foreigner-friendly
reviews.text: They charge extra 3% when paying with foreign-issued cards (in Indonesia, I hear it’s the same for Philippines and Thailand, and Vietnam is 4%?). I KNOW that processing domestic and foreign cards incurs different costs on merchants, this is true around the world, but is the difference REALLY 3% in Indonesia? I have a suspicion it really might cost Grab around 1%, more or less, to charge my card vs. an Indonesian debit card, but they up it to 3% in order to profit off tourists. I see this mentality a lot in certain tourist-dependent locations, where they try to get any extra profit they can off foreign tourists so hard, they end up looking like sleazy scammers. Too bad Grab, which positions themselves as “progressive” and “next generation”, is following this pattern.
